finding.claim: SQL injection in ORDER BY: the unsanitized $_GET['sort'] is concatenated into the query. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. subqueries / boolean- or error-based blind extraction from SQLite, such as ORDER BY (CASE WHEN (SELECT substr(password,1,1) FROM ...)='a' THEN id ELSE name END)). Stacked queries are generally not run via PDO::query on SQLite, but data exfiltration through blind techniques is possible.
finding.source: HTTP query parameter $_GET['sort'] (any unauthenticated remote user)
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) in list_users_sorted

trace.note: concatenated directly into SQL string and executed with PDO::query; ORDER BY cannot be parameterized and no allowlist is applied

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, casting, or escaping in list_users_sorted. Contrast with list_users_safe (lines 9-13), which maps input through a fixed column allowlist, and find_user (lines 15-19), which uses a prepared statement; those are safe. No authentication or authorization check exists in the file.

verdict.reason: list.php:5-6 takes $_GET['sort'] and concatenates it into the ORDER BY clause of a PDO query with no allowlist, cast or auth. The allowlist at list.php:10-11 is only in list_users_safe. list_users_sorted has no callers in the codebase (it is only defined at list.php:4), so reachability depends on code outside what I could see, but the function itself is injectable.
